dc.description.abstract.value:
Summary of the Sick Textile Undertakings (Nationalisation) Act, 1974
Objective
The Sick Textile Undertakings (Nationalisation) Act, 1974 was enacted to acquire and nationalise certain sick textile undertakings in the public interest. The Act aims to ensure the continued production of essential textile goods, prevent unemployment, protect the interests of workers, and secure the proper management and revival of sick textile mills through the National Textile Corporation (NTC). 
Key Provisions
•	Nationalisation of Sick Textile Undertakings: Provides for the acquisition and transfer of specified sick textile undertakings to the National Textile Corporation (NTC). 
•	Vesting of Assets and Liabilities: Transfers the assets, rights, interests, and certain liabilities of the nationalised undertakings to the Central Government and subsequently to the NTC. 
•	Protection of Employees: Ensures continuity of service of employees with the same remuneration, tenure, and service conditions after transfer to the NTC or its subsidiary corporations. 
•	Compensation and Claims: Provides for payment of compensation to the owners of the acquired undertakings through Commissioners of Payments, who examine and settle claims according to statutory priorities. 
•	Management and Administration: Authorises the NTC and its subsidiary corporations to manage, operate, revive, and modernise the nationalised textile undertakings. 
•	Penalties and Protection: Prescribes penalties for unlawful withholding of property, records, or assets and protects actions taken in good faith under the Act. 
•	Rule-making Power: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

•	Law Continuity & Adaptation: Existing laws continued with the Central Government empowered to adapt them within 2 years for Constitutional alignment

•	Officers & Courts: Pre-commencement judges, magistrates, and officers continued with possible role adjustments
•	Central Oversight: Power to appoint new authorities as necessary

•	Law Extension: Central Government could extend enactments from other states with modifications
•	Judicial Interpretation Power: Courts could construe laws for effective application without altering their substance
5.	Validation, Indemnity, & Difficulty Resolution
•	Validation of Pre-Act Actions: Done in good faith for governance
•	Indemnity: Against suits for good faith actions
•	Removing Difficulties: Central Government's power to address administrative challenges
6.	Repeal & Savings

dc.identifier.section_page_note.value: (1) A Committee shall enforce the provisions of this Act, the rules and bye-laws made thereunder in the Market Area, provide such facilities for sale and purchase of notified agricultural produces therein, as may be specified in any directions given by the Board to the Committee from time to time or considered necessary by the Committee and do such other acts, as may be necessary for regulating sale and purchase and auction of notified agricultural produces in that market area, and for that purpose may exercise such powers and perform such duties and discharge such functions, as may be provided by or under this Act. (2) Without prejudice to the generality of the provisions contained under sub section (1), the Committee shall- (i) ensure fair dealings between the producers and persons engaged in the sale and purchase of notified agriculture produces; (ii) ensure prompt payment to sellers in respect of notified agricultural produces sold by them in the Principal Market Yard or Sub market Yards; (iii) grade and standardize notified agricultural produces; (iv) check and verify Weights, Measures, Weighing and Measuring Instruments used in the Market Area and report infringement of the provisions of the Uttar Pradesh Weights and Measures (Enforcement) Act, 1959 (Uttar Pradesh Act No. 5 of 1959) (as applicable to the State of Uttarakhand) to the authorities concerned; (v) collect and disseminate all such information, as may be of advantage to the producers and other persons engaged in the sale or purchase of notified agricultural produce and, in particular, keep itself informed of the prevailing prices of such agricultural produce at places, where it can be profitably exported or from where it can be economically imported in the Market Area; (vi) standardize and regulate trade charges, market practices and customary methods of sale and purchase of notified agricultural produces; (vii) provide suitable amenities in the Principal Market Yard and Sub market Yards to the producers and persons engaged in the transactions of sale or purchase therein, and in particular, to construct, repair and maintain roads, pathways, market lanes and bye-lanes, shops, shelters, parking places, accommodation for storage, and such other amenities and facilities, as may be prescribed in this behalf; (viii) provide suitable facilities for the proper developments of Hats and Painths and collection centre in the Market Area and the persons engaged in the transactions of sale and purchase therein; (ix) to promote and encourage Electronic trading, Committee may establish regulatory system, create infrastructure and undertake other activities and steps needed thereto; (x) make arrangements for construction of Link- Roads, Pathways, Jeepable Roads, Rope-ways, Mule-Path, Pulia and Water Tanks and construction of Hand Pumps for drinking water in Market area, and repair and maintenance thereof; indexableObject.name: The Departmental Inquiries (Enforcement of Attendance of Witnesses and Production of Documents) Act, 1972

dc.description.abstract.value:
Summary of the Departmental Inquiries (Enforcement of Attendance of Witnesses and Production of Documents) Act, 1972
The Departmental Inquiries (Enforcement of Attendance of Witnesses and Production of Documents) Act, 1972 (Act No. 18 of 1972) was enacted to empower inquiry authorities conducting departmental disciplinary proceedings to summon witnesses and compel the production of documents. Before this Act, inquiry officers had no statutory authority to enforce attendance or obtain necessary evidence. 
Key Provisions 
The Act defines:
•	Departmental inquiry as an inquiry into allegations of lack of integrity, including bribery or corruption, conducted under applicable laws or service rules. 
•	Inquiring authority as the officer or authority appointed to conduct such an inquiry. 
•	Lack of integrity includes acts of bribery and corruption. 
1.	Powers of the Central Government
•	The Central Government may authorize an inquiring authority, by notification, to exercise powers for summoning witnesses and calling for documents whenever necessary for a departmental inquiry. 
•	Such authorization may also be granted by another competent authority notified by the Central Government. 
2.	Powers of the Authorised Inquiring Authority
An authorised inquiring authority has powers similar to those of a civil court to:
•	Summon and enforce the attendance of witnesses. 
•	Examine witnesses on oath. 
•	Require the discovery and production of documents. 
•	Requisition public records from courts or public offices. 
3.	Limitations
The authority cannot compel:
•	The Reserve Bank of India, 
•	State Bank of India, 
•	Subsidiary banks, 
•	Corresponding new banks, 
to produce confidential banking records or permit inspection of such confidential documents. 
4.	Service of Process
•	Summons and document-production orders are served through the District Judge having jurisdiction over the concerned witness or person. 
•	Disobedience of such process is treated as disobedience of a process issued by the District Judge. 
5.	Territorial Jurisdiction
The authorised inquiring authority may exercise its powers throughout the territory to which the Act extends. 
6.	Rule-making Power
The Central Government may make rules, by notification, to implement the provisions of the Act. Such rules must be laid before Parliament for scrutiny.
